subject: Q3 trajectory adjustment & cross-team handoffs — decision request
messages:
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 11 Oct 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Q3 trajectory adjustment & cross-team handoffs — decision request

Team —

Quick mid-run update and a decision ask for the QBR pack. Attached is the latest Q3_OKR_heatmap_v3 (tabbed view per initiative) and a proposed canary_deploy_plan_v2 that maps the rollout dependencies. High level: we are tracking mixed across the three platform-facing OKRs and I recommend a small, surgical re-scope of one throughput target to prioritize reliability work that is currently blocking customer-facing milestones.

Summary (TL;DR):
- Recommend shifting "Reduce p99 inference tail" target from 35% unit improvement to a 20% committed improvement for Q3, moving remaining work into a Q4 carryover.
- To do this safely we need two immediate cross-team commitments: an infra slot for a week-long kernel optimization window (INF-1428) and a CS-run canary on the top 10 enterprise routes.
- Impact: preserves release cadence for Hosted API customers and avoids a larger rollback risk to Dedicated customers.

What I need from each of you by EOD Wed (10/13):
- Marcus: confirm availability of 4 engineer-weeks from Serving Runtime (or name alternates) and whether INF-1428 can be scheduled the week of 10/19.
- Naomi: confirm coverage plan for the customer canary (SLOs to watch, who runs the throttle tests) and whether we can compress the QBR artifact for the reliability appendix.
- Rishi: assess whether the proposed re-scope changes the commit language we send to sales/finance (discounting/credits) and whether we need an exec note for customers.

Why this approach: we have a high confidence win if we prioritize the kernel hot path and run canaries early. The attached heatmap shows the tradeoffs by customer tier. I want to avoid a broad scope cut that would risk visibility metrics in the QBR.

Notes on attachments: the heatmap has a "recommended cut" column with per-initiative impact; the canary plan has rollback gates and suggested thresholds.

Thanks — please reply inline. I plan to capture decisions in the QBR deck on Thursday.

—
Evelyn Hart
Director, Product Strategy
Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 11 Oct 2026 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Q3 trajectory adjustment & cross-team handoffs — decision request

Evelyn —

Thanks for the concise ask and the artifacts. Quick answers:
- Serving Runtime can allocate the equivalent of 4 engineer-weeks. I propose: 2 weeks for kernel optimization (pairing runtime + infra), 1 week for KV cache tuning, 1 week for validation and benchmarking. Engineers: Priya (lead), Daniel, and a short-term contractor I can onboard for the validation sprint.
- INF-1428: we have a 10/19 window available; will confirm by EOD tomorrow after snagging infra reservations. If infra pushes it out, alternative is 10/26 but that increases QBR risk.

Risks/asks:
- We will need priority access to the dedicated GPU pool for at least the validation week — Naomi, can CS/ops ensure a throttle schedule so we don't collide with customer tests?
- If we compress the metrics window (e.g., move to 48h canary vs 72h), we'll lose some statistical confidence; recommend keeping 72h if feasible.

I can join the canary run and help instrument traces. If everyone is good, I will mark the INF ticket with owners and tentative dates tonight.

-Marcus
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 11 Oct 2026 15:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Q3 trajectory adjustment & cross-team handoffs — decision request

On Mon, Oct 11, 2026 at 10:03 AM Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com> wrote:
> Evelyn —
>
> Thanks for the concise ask and the artifacts. Quick answers:
> - Serving Runtime can allocate the equivalent of 4 engineer-weeks...

Folks —

I support the surgical re-scope; reliability issues are affecting two named enterprise customers and buying runway here makes sense. Operational notes:
- CS can run the canary but we need clear playbooks. I'll draft a short checklist (who executes, monitoring dashboard widgets, and rollback criteria). Expect a first draft by Tue evening.
- On GPU reservations: we can provide a reduced pool (2 nodes) for the validation week, but not the full dedicated pool unless we shift lower-priority infra tests. If Marcus's team can accept partial capacity (2 nodes + simulated load), we can proceed without moving other customer tests.
- QBR artifacts: I can compress the reliability appendix to a 2-slide callout if we commit to the 72h canary. If we do 48h, I will need one additional slide explaining confidence limitations.

One open ask for leadership: if we are reducing the p99 improvement target, can we signal that to Sales with a short note (one paragraph) that frames this as a quality-first decision? Rishi, can you draft or advise?

-Naomi
Head of Customer Reliability

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 12 Oct 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Q3 trajectory adjustment & cross-team handoffs — decision request

Evelyn / team —

Thanks for pulling this together. Quick summary of decisions and next steps from my side: 
- Decision accepted: reduce p99 improvement target to 20% for Q3 and carry remainder into Q4. I'll prepare a one-paragraph message for Sales that frames the change as "quality-first, reduces customer risk" and include a short FAQ for top enterprise accounts.
- Financial impact: minimal for Q3 unless we fail the canary and require credits; I'll flag that as a contingent risk and coordinate with Finance if the canary shows regressions.
- I'll send the Sales note and FAQ draft by EOD Wed 10/13 and echo to Legal if there's material contract language to adjust.

Action items captured: 
1) Marcus: confirm INF-1428 schedule (target 10/19) and owner list — due EOD Tue 10/12 (if not possible, notify immediately).
2) Naomi: draft canary playbook and monitoring widgets — first draft due Tue 10/13.
3) Evelyn: finalize QBR deck appendix and include the short Sales note — due Thu 10/14.

I'll also add a short call on Wednesday 10/13 at 9:30am PT if we need a quick alignment. Otherwise, proceed with the plan above.

-Rishi
VP, Revenue Operations
